deep_dive.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
deep_dive.abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 深度基础模型多输出仿射不变的相对深度，其在新场景中的泛化性与尺度仍不明确，限制了机器人几何感知。本文提出EM-ViT单目深度估计模型，借助视差细化与机器人自运动在线把基础模型的相对深度自适应校准到度量尺度。实验表明该方法能在陌生非结构化环境中给出稠密长距离的度量深度，减少对激光雷达与双目相机的依赖，为真实机器人场景下的深度先验提供了更可用的方案。

deep_dive.title: EG360: Efficient and Generalizable $360^\circ$ Depth Estimation via Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation and Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion
deep_dive.abstract: Generalized panorama depth estimation has witnessed great advances in recent years. These methods typically achieve robust zero-shot generalization performance using large pretrained models, but their high computational cost makes real-time inference on embedded platforms challenging. In contrast, previous lightweight panorama models have mostly been developed for single-domain evaluations and cannot generalize well due to domain shifts. To reduce the gap between these two types of models, we introduce EG360, an efficient and generalizable panorama depth estimation model. Specifically, building on a lightweight depth model, we design an Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation (APPD) strategy guided by scene geometry, along with a Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion (SCFF) module for global semantic perception. As a result, with only 6.593M parameters after reparameterization, EG360 achieves strong zero-shot performance on real-world benchmarks and runs at 35 FPS on a Jetson Orin NX 16GB in MAXN mode, whereas a previous ViT-small model runs at less than 2 FPS. Our code will also be made public for future research.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对全景深度估计中大型预训练模型计算开销大、轻量模型跨域泛化差的问题，本文提出EG360高效可泛化全景深度估计模型。方法以轻量深度模型为基础，设计自适应全景-透视蒸馏和球面跨层特征融合，以兼顾精度、效率与跨域泛化能力。该工作旨在缩小大模型与轻量模型之间的差距，使嵌入式平台上的实时深度推理更可行，并为资源受限场景下的零样本深度估计提供新思路。

quick_skim.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
quick_skim.abstract: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons about and understands the image and its depth at the same time, and one set of weights generates images with their depth, estimates depth from photographs and paints images onto a given depth. At enough scale it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists on established depth benchmarks while keeping the generative abilities of the backbone it started from without specialized layers. We release two models for the community.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Iris-Z proposes a unified generative image model that jointly produces appearance and geometry, aiming to replace task-specific monocular geometry architectures. On monocular geometry it surpasses specialist models, supporting a foundation-model path for visual geometry.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对单目几何任务长期依赖专用架构的问题，本文提出Iris-Z统一图像生成器，在单一骨干中同时生成外观与几何，并用同一生成训练任务覆盖多种几何理解。作者在单目几何任务上验证该通用模型能够超越专用几何模型，且性能随数据、参数和计算规模持续提升。该工作说明通用生成式基础模型有望替代任务专用设计，为视觉几何理解提供可扩展的新路径。

quick_skim.title: Kosmo-GFM: A Production-Ready Geometry Foundation Model
quick_skim.abstract: We present Kosmo-GFM, a scene reconstruction system that integrates a geometry foundation model (GFM), a pose optimization engine (PoseEngine), and reconstruction-derived supervision from KosmoWorld. GFM predicts camera parameters, depth, cross-view correspondences, and dynamic 3D points from images and videos. PoseEngine combines these predictions with geometric optimization to recover scene-level camera poses and geometry for downstream 3D and 4D Gaussian Splatting. KosmoWorld generates images and geometric supervision from reconstructed real-world scenes to improve GFM's geometric predictions. On the Sparse and Medium subsets of SpatialBench, GFM achieves the lowest absolute relative depth error and the highest relative-pose AUC at 5 degrees among the compared methods. It also achieves the lowest mean endpoint errors for dynamic points and scene flow across the five evaluated datasets. Across 34 scenes completed by all compared reconstruction systems, PoseEngine achieves the highest scene-averaged pose AUC at thresholds of 1, 3, and 5 degrees, with a cumulative runtime of 14.07 hours, approximately 20% of GLUEMAP's 69.67 hours. PoseEngine Flash provides a further accuracy-efficiency trade-off, with a measured mixed-precision runtime of 2.62 hours, approximately 4% of GLUEMAP's runtime. Separate scaling experiments show generally favorable trends with increased data, model computation, and training budgets. These results support the use of learned geometric priors within a scene-level reconstruction pipeline.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有场景重建需同时获得相机参数与深度几何。本文提出Kosmo-GFM系统，整合几何基础模型、位姿优化引擎与基于重建的监督数据，从图像视频中预测相机参数、深度、跨视图对应与动态三维点。在SpatialBench上其绝对相对深度误差最低、相对位姿AUC最高，为下游三维重建提供了通用深度基础模型。
